slot.brief: Use Euler-type substitution t = x + √(x² + k) to rationalise and integrate an expression with √(x² + k).

verdicts.working: Let t=x+√(x²+3), so dx/√(x²+3)=dt/t. The bounds become t=2 and t=3. Then ∫₂³ dt/[t(t+1)(t+2)] = [½ln t−ln(t+1)+½ln(t+2)]₂³ = ½ln(135/128).

working:
Let $t=x+\sqrt{x^2+3}$. Then $x=\dfrac{t^2-3}{2t}$ and $\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2+3}}=\dfrac{dt}{t}$. The limits become $t=2,3$, so $I=\displaystyle\int_2^3\dfrac{dt}{t(t+1)(t+2)}=\displaystyle\int_2^3\left(\dfrac{1}{2t}-\dfrac{1}{t+1}+\dfrac{1}{2(t+2)}\right)dt=\dfrac12\ln\left(\dfrac{135}{128}\right)$.

Independent check: Let t=x+√(x²+3), so dx/√(x²+3)=dt/t. The bounds become t=2 and t=3. Then ∫₂³ dt/[t(t+1)(t+2)] = [½ln t−ln(t+1)+½ln(t+2)]₂³ = ½ln(135/128).
